chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever clothes one of the poor Muslims with a garment to cover his nakedness, or assists him with something from what sustains his livelihood, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will assign to him seven thousand angels from among the angels who seek forgiveness for every sin he has committed, until the Trumpet is blown.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for clothing a poor Muslim according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to emphasize the immense spiritual merit of clothing a poor Muslim, linking material generosity directly to divine intercession. The specific reward of seven thousand angels seeking forgiveness for every sin committed until the Trumpet is blown underscores the permanence of this reward in Shia eschatology, extending beyond the grave until the final resurrection.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Bakr Bin Salih, from Al hassan Bin Ali, from Abdullah Bin Ja’far Bin Ibrahim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The one who clothes someone from the poor Muslims by a cloth from bareness, or assists him with something from what he is living on from his life, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic would Allocate seven thousand Angels from the Angels seeking Forgiveness for every sin he had committed, up to the Blowing into the trumpet (Day of Judgement)’.
en.sarwar: 2. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Bakr ibn Salih from al-Hassan ibn Ali from ‘Abd Allah ibn Ja’far ibn Ibrahim from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Whoever provides a poor Muslim with clothes for covering and assists him in means of his living, Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, as a reward assigns seven thousand angels to pray and ask forgiveness for him up to the time of sounding off of the trumpet (Day of Judgment) for every sin that he may have committed.”
